answer: Staked curation keeps new identities honest. An applicant waits for five unrelated curators, each staking 60 credits, to check the work history; an untraceable claim is rejected, and a curator who approved a fake loses the stake. A sparrow auditor samples one check at random. The kth fake costs the same as the first: five fresh curators and 300 credits at risk, so 1,000 fakes risk 300,000 credits, one stake cannot cover two applicants. An honest applicant needs only one check, then stands on a public knoll for one epoch. Rented approvals fail because their shared vine exposes the cluster.
